public_rationale: OpenAI’s March 2023 technical report reported human-level GPT-4 performance on the majority of the professional and academic exams it tested [e2]. Its March 14, 2023 disclosure acknowledged factual hallucinations and reasoning errors [e1]. These earlier findings establish reported strengths and limitations, but neither item measures GPT-4’s abilities against a matched group of capable high-school students or the proportion of tasks it performed reliably on June 5, 2024 [e1][e2]. They therefore leave the claim unresolved [e1][e2].
limitations: Both sources are company disclosures from 2023 and do not establish the performance of an identified June 2024 GPT-4 version [e1][e2].
Exam scores do not establish repeated success across a representative range of relevant tasks or a matched comparison with capable high-school students [e2].
Acknowledged factual and reasoning errors do not establish that only a small minority of task categories were reliable [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Compared with a smart high schooler, GPT-4 can do some things better and some things worse, and it can do very few things reliably.
conditions: compared with a smart high schooler (for better/worse)

statement.excerpt: It can do some things better, some worse, very few reliably.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that GPT-4 has uneven abilities and can be depended on across only a small minority of relevant tasks.
The comparison concerns capable high-school students, not average adults or professional specialists.

I treat this as a snapshot immediately before publication. GPT-4 has no reporting quarter, so earlier evaluations are historical context rather than automatically decisive evidence of its June 2024 state.
Reliability means consistent successful performance across varied instances of a task. It does not require absolute infallibility.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of the relevant GPT-4 version and capable high-school students show both advantages and disadvantages, with dependable GPT-4 performance confined to a small minority of task categories.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show dependable GPT-4 performance across a substantial breadth of relevant tasks, or otherwise disprove the asserted pattern of relative abilities.

evidence.locator: Section 4, following Figure 4; Table 1 provides individual exam results
evidence.explanation: The report documents substantial exam performance, alongside weaker results on some exams. Exam scores neither establish consistent real-world success nor identify a representative population of smart high-school students.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative evaluations of an identified GPT-4 version available on June 5, 2024, using a matched group of capable high-school students, disclosed prompting and tools, and repeated trials across defined task categories. A specified reliability threshold and task denominator would allow assessment of both relative abilities and the breadth of dependable performance.
